Let \(S=\Pi+B+\Gamma\). Since the digits are distinct and \(\Pi\neq 0\),  
\[
10\le S\le 9+8+7=24.
\]
Also
\[
100\Pi+10B+\Gamma=S(S+1).
\]
Check \(S=10,11,\dots,24\). The only value where \(S(S+1)\) has digit sum \(S\) and distinct digits is
\[
S=12,\qquad 12\cdot 13=156.
\]
Indeed, \(1+5+6=12\), and digits are distinct.

\[
\boxed{156}
\]
